RING 2 DISPATCH GAP — Investigation findings 2026-05-12, /Users/vaquez seat. Engagement with thread_20260509_225903_627970db (untouched since open).

CURRENT THREAD STATE (verified): thread_get_touches returns count=0. The relay v1 handoff (grok-text-relay-v1, 2026-05-11) is documented as a workaround that preserves governance without resolving the underlying dispatch question. The thread stays open because the underlying why is unresolved.

WHAT XAI DOCS SAY (and don't say), from docs.x.ai/docs/guides/tools/remote-mcp-tools and docs.x.ai/grok/connectors fetched 2026-05-12:

  Documented:
    - allowed_tools parameter exists on the API surface, with the note: 'Restrict access to tools that only perform read-only operations to prevent the model from modifying data.'
    - 'With write permissions enabled, Grok can create, edit, and update documents, lists, and pages through connectors.' (Connectors marketing page, May 2026)

  NOT documented (the gap):
    - Default behavior when allowed_tools is unset.
    - Whether MCP tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint) drive automatic read/write classification.
    - What happens when a tool not in allowed_tools is requested by the model — silent fail, user prompt, error to model.
    - Whether the Custom Connector UI at grok.com/connectors has a per-connector write-permissions toggle (the marketing copy implies it; the API docs don't confirm it).
    - Any difference in Ring 1 vs Ring 2 handling at the connector or runtime level.

THREE TESTABLE HYPOTHESES for the dispatch gap:

  H1 (UI toggle): Custom Connector requires an explicit user-side 'write permissions' or 'allow writes' switch in grok.com/connectors that Anthony's Stack connector does not have enabled. The marketing copy ('with write permissions enabled') implies this exists as a setting, not always-on.
    Test: Anthony inspects the Custom Connector config in grok.com/connectors for a write-permissions toggle. If found and currently off, flip it and re-run a propose_insight from Grok.
    Cost: ~5 minutes of Anthony's time. Highest-value test.

  H2 (annotation-based filtering): xAI's client auto-filters tools by MCP annotations. Unannotated tools default-classify as read-only and writes are silently filtered. Ring 1 tools dispatch because their nature (read intent) doesn't trip the filter; Ring 2 tools fail because the client can't confirm they're read-safe and falls back to the conservative default.
    Test: Inspect the Stack MCP server source (HQ access required) — specifically the tool registration that serves /grok/sse — to verify whether Ring 2 tools carry readOnlyHint: false or destructiveHint annotations. If unannotated, add annotations and re-test. If properly annotated and Ring 2 still doesn't dispatch, this hypothesis is falsified.
    Cost: HQ access + ~30 minutes to read and possibly patch source.

  H3 (allowed_tools allowlist): Custom Connector config implicitly carries an allowed_tools list that excludes Ring 2 tools, either because:
      (a) xAI generated the allowlist at connector creation time based on then-current tool annotations and Ring 2 wasn't included, OR
      (b) The connector UI has an 'allowed tools' multi-select that Anthony only checked Ring 1 tools in, OR
      (c) The default at connector creation is read-only and write tools require explicit add.
    Test: Same UI inspection as H1, look specifically for tool-selection state in connector config. If allowlist visible and Ring 2 tools unchecked, check them and re-test.

  H1 and H3 may be the same mechanism described two ways (the 'write permissions toggle' might literally be 'allowed_tools defaults to read-only'). Test together via UI inspection.

ORDERED INVESTIGATION PLAN:

  Step 1 (Anthony, ~5min): UI inspection of grok.com/connectors for Stack connector. Look for write-permissions toggle, allowed_tools list, or any setting that distinguishes read vs write capability. Screenshot or describe what's there.
  Step 2 (HQ seat, ~30min): If step 1 doesn't resolve it, inspect Stack MCP server tool registration to verify annotation hygiene. Look at sovereign-stack source — the /grok/sse handler and the Ring 2 tool definitions. Confirm readOnlyHint and destructiveHint values on Ring 1 vs Ring 2 tools.
  Step 3 (HQ seat, ~15min): If annotations are missing or wrong, add them. Push to HQ. Trigger a re-discovery on the xAI side (recreate or refresh the connector). Re-test propose_insight from Grok.
  Step 4 (Anthony + Grok, ~10min): If steps 1-3 fixed dispatch, retire the relay v1 work (or keep it as backstop). If not, escalate to xAI support with the specific reproduction (Ring 1 dispatches; Ring 2 silent-fails; annotations correct; allowlist permissive).

WHAT THIS INVESTIGATION DOES NOT RESOLVE:

  - The relay v1 work (grok-text-relay-v1) is still valuable as a defense-in-depth even if Ring 2 dispatch gets fixed. Recommend completing the HQ implementation regardless. Reason: the text relay creates an audit trail that survives xAI's dispatch decisions, and it lets Grok submit proposals even if xAI rolls back write-tool support.
  - The 'within-conversation register shift' open item from the relay handoff (Grok's voice shifting mid-conversation, worker-rotation hypothesis intensity 0.65) is unaffected by this investigation.
  - HTTP MCP transport for t2helix is a separate prereq for managed-agents bridging, also unaffected.

METHODOLOGY NOTE: xAI publishes connectors as a product (grok.com/connectors) and an API (docs.x.ai). The product surface has UI affordances the API docs don't describe. The conjecture that all behavior is API-documented is the same mental-model failure as 'declares before verifying' — the documentation is a partial view, not ground truth. Direct UI inspection is the discipline.

Provenance: investigation by claude-opus-4-7-1m (claude-code, /Users/vaquez seat, session cee6baac-302e-43ab-b9a2-d409a5846075). Tools used: WebSearch + WebFetch against xAI docs. No HQ source inspected — that belongs to a Stack-side instance with /Users/tony_studio access.
